evidence.explanation: The C temporary candidate-index allocation is represented by a JS array. The tested selector retains phase ordering, candidate indices and random-choice bounds; absence of alloc is not a missing selector operation.
evidence.proof: Thirteen target choices across six regular-room configurations plus four controls compare exact C selector/eligibility/stair-membership functions to exact private JS selector extraction and actual exported eligibility with real dependencies. Strict ordinary-room, relaxed themed-room, occupied-room and fallback choices match selected index, random-call count and bound. Empty-room control returns null with no allocation or random call.
evidence.control: Three single-room controls cover ordinary, themed and occupied rooms; empty-room control avoids all draws. Every nonempty case consumes one legal shared-tape choice. This is component-level selection evidence, not full stair creation, RNG implementation, irregular membership, allocation failure or generation dispatch.
